scenes.title: Pivot
scenes.narration: Pivoting reshapes data by turning rows into columns, converting a long, narrow result into a wide summary.

scenes.title: What pivoting does
bullets: Rotates distinct row values into separate columns
Transforms long format into wide format
Usually pairs a grouping key with an aggregate
scenes.narration: Pivoting rotates the distinct values found in one column into separate columns of their own. In doing so it transforms long format, with many rows per key, into wide format with one row per key. It almost always pairs a grouping key with an aggregate such as a sum or a count.

scenes.title: Pivot with conditional aggregation
scenes.code:
SELECT
    product,
    SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q1' THEN amount END) AS q1,
    SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q2' THEN amount END) AS q2,
    SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q3' THEN amount END) AS q3,
    SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q4' THEN amount END) AS q4
FROM sales
GROUP BY product;
scenes.narration: The portable way to pivot is conditional aggregation. We group by product to get one row per product. Each CASE expression isolates the amount for a single quarter, and SUM collapses those into one value per column. The result gives each product a row with four quarterly totals across the columns.

scenes.title: Two approaches

left.title: Conditional aggregation
points: Works in virtually every SQL engine
You spell out each output column
Full control over naming and logic

right.title: PIVOT operator
points: Available in SQL Server and Oracle
Column list still fixed at write time

scenes.narration: Conditional aggregation with CASE works in virtually every engine and gives you full control, at the cost of spelling out each column. Some engines like SQL Server and Oracle offer a dedicated PIVOT operator that is more compact for simple cases, though you still fix the column list when you write the query.

scenes.text: To pivot, group by the row key and use one SUM(CASE WHEN ...) per target column — portable, explicit, and easy to read.
scenes.narration: To pivot, group by the row key and write one SUM with a CASE expression per target column; it is portable, explicit, and easy for the next person to read.
